This Pull Request has been created to fix #52643 

### Detail

This Pull Request changes

**Original**
https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/16882b886e245f363cd61f5ea553fe2bc525d070/activerecord/lib/active_record/relation/query_methods.rb#L1624

**Modified**

```ruby
elsif opts.include?("?") && rest.compact.present?
```

To make sure for the nil value of the rest we are constructing the query 
```ruby
"SELECT \"users\".* FROM \"users\" WHERE (LOWER(name) IS NULL) LIMIT $1"
```

Instead of 
```ruby
"SELECT \"users\".* FROM \"users\" WHERE (LOWER(name) IS $1) LIMIT $2"
```

issue_context.title: PG::SyntaxError on query serialize in Rails 7.2
issue_context.body:
### Description
Problem with serialization sql query with string condition and `nil` bind value with PostgreSQL adapter (it does work with sqlite3) 

### Steps to reproduce
```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'bundler/inline'

gemfile(true) do
  source 'https://rubygems.org'

  gem 'rails'
  # If you want to test against edge Rails replace the previous line with this:
  # gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"

  gem 'pg'
end

require 'active_record'
require 'minitest/autorun'
require 'logger'

db_config = { adapter: 'postgresql', database: 'test', host: 'localhost' }
ActiveRecord::Tasks::DatabaseTasks.create(db_config)

# This connection will do for database-independent bug reports.
ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: 'postgresql', database: 'test')
ActiveRecord::Base.logger = Logger.new($stdout)

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :users, force: true do |t|
    t.string :name
  end
end

class User < ActiveRecord::Base
end

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_association_stuff
    user1 = User.create!(name: 'John Doe')
    user2 = User.create!

    assert_equal user1, User.find_by('LOWER(name) = ?', 'john doe')
    assert_equal nil, User.find_by('LOWER(name) = ?', 'jane doe')
    assert_equal user2, User.find_by('LOWER(name) IS ?', nil)
  end
end
```

### Expected behavior
Serialize query with `LOWER(name) IS NULL` condition

### Actual behavior
```
ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid: PG::SyntaxError: ERROR:  syntax error at or near "$1"
LINE 1: ...LECT "users".* FROM "users" WHERE (LOWER(name) IS $1) LIMIT ...
```

### System configuration
**Rails version**:
Rails 7.2.0
**Ruby version**:
ruby 3.3.4 (2024-07-09 revision be1089c8ec) [arm64-darwin23]
comments:
Using `git bisect`

https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/8e6a5deca626c944933211d7977f4e7e76869e74 is the first bad commit

Rails version: ">=v7.2.0" introduced the bug.

cc: @byroot
With MySQL and Sqlite3 functionality is working as expected.

The following line is giving different SQL

https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/16882b886e245f363cd61f5ea553fe2bc525d070/activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/abstract/database_statements.rb#L34

**Before**
```ruby
"SELECT \"users\".* FROM \"users\" WHERE (LOWER(name) IS NULL) LIMIT $1"
```

**>=7.2.0**

```ruby
"SELECT \"users\".* FROM \"users\" WHERE (LOWER(name) IS $1) LIMIT $2"
```

`arel_or_sql_string` value is

**Before**

```ruby
#<Arel::Nodes::SelectStatement:0x0000000137892370 @cores=[#<Arel::Nodes::SelectCore:0x00000001374bed98 @source=#<Arel::Nodes::JoinSource:0x00000001528350b0 @left=#<Arel::Table:0x00000001209f01e8 @name="users", @klass=User(id: integer, name: string), @type_caster=#<ActiveRecord::TypeCaster::Map:0x0000000150752528 @klass=User(id: integer, name: string)>, @table_alias=nil>, @right=[]>, @set_quantifier=nil, @optimizer_hints=nil, @projections=[#<struct Arel::Attributes::Attribute relation=#<Arel::Table:0x00000001209f01e8 @name="users", @klass=User(id: integer, name: string), @type_caster=#<ActiveRecord::TypeCaster::Map:0x0000000150752528 @klass=User(id: integer, name: string)>, @table_alias=nil>, name="*">], @wheres=[#<Arel::Nodes::Grouping:0x0000000152834a48 @expr="LOWER(name) IS NULL">], @groups=[], @havings=[], @windows=[], @comment=nil>], @orders=[], @limit=#<Arel::Nodes::Limit:0x00000001528349a8 @expr=#<ActiveModel::Attribute::WithCastValue:0x00000001378922d0 @name="LIMIT", @value_before_type_cast=1, @type=#<ActiveModel::Type::Value:0x00000001506bdea0 @precision=nil, @scale=nil, @limit=nil>, @original_attribute=nil>>, @lock=nil, @offset=nil, @with=nil>
```

**>=7.2.0**
```ruby
#<Arel::Nodes::SelectStatement:0x00000001347b89e8 @cores=[#<Arel::Nodes::SelectCore:0x0000000123d54a70 @source=#<Arel::Nodes::JoinSource:0x00000001342dd090 @left=#<Arel::Table:0x00000001350fdf30 @name="users", @klass=User(id: integer, name: string), @type_caster=#<ActiveRecord::TypeCaster::Map:0x00000001340fb330 @klass=User(id: integer, name: string)>, @table_alias=nil>, @right=[]>, @set_quantifier=nil, @optimizer_hints=nil, @projections=[#<struct Arel::Attributes::Attribute relation=#<Arel::Table:0x00000001350fdf30 @name="users", @klass=User(id: integer, name: string), @type_caster=#<ActiveRecord::TypeCaster::Map:0x00000001340fb330 @klass=User(id: integer, name: string)>, @table_alias=nil>, name="*">], @wheres=[#<Arel::Nodes::BoundSqlLiteral "(LOWER(name) IS ?)" [nil]>], @groups=[], @havings=[], @windows=[], @comment=nil>], @orders=[], @limit=#<Arel::Nodes::Limit:0x00000001342dca00 @expr=#<ActiveModel::Attribute::WithCastValue:0x00000001347b88f8 @name="LIMIT", @value_before_type_cast=1, @type=#<ActiveModel::Type::Value:0x0000000134331960 @precision=nil, @scale=nil, @limit=nil>, @original_attribute=nil>>, @lock=nil, @offset=nil, @with=nil>
```

After a quick search it appears that Postgresql don't support `"IS $1", [nil]`. It worked previously because these fragments where eagerly interpolated rather than properly prepared.

I think I can restore that behavior when the bound value is NULL, but, even if I know the example is contrivied for reproduction purposes, given that the only valid value to pass to `"name is ?"` is `nil`, I'd change that code to just not take a parameter.

> I think I can restore that behavior when the bound value is NULL

Actually, I'm afraid I can't. The problem isn't the bound value, it's the query itself, and parsing the query would be too unreliable. 

I get how this is a bit of a regression in your specific case, but the advantages far out-weight that one case. So I'll be closing as wontfix, but if someone has an idea how to handle this case, feel free to open a PR.

Sorry.

For anyone who also had this issue: I was able to get around it by using `Arel.sql("NULL") in place of `nil` in the params, so if I'm using a where statement, it looks like:
```ruby
User.where('LOWER(name) IS ?', Arel.sql("NULL"))
```

Note that using a string `"NULL"` (instead of the Arel statement) will not avoid the issue.
@byroot its an excellent question. Short answer - no.  the rest of my scopes are like that.  Something tells me it was some legacy code.  Regardless, it still should support it.

I should probably have clarified in my comment above that we had a complex query that if refactored to use the `where.and`, `where.not`, `where.or` methods with a `joins` would resulted in a `where.or` that threw an error because the relations passed were not [structurally compatible](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/e1d58cfd05ae1cc0bfc1006b7ce973a7730831df/activerecord/lib/active_record/relation/query_methods.rb#L1155).

Also, legacy being legacy, it was better that I was able to find a workaround that only required me to change the param from `nil` to `Arel.sql("NULL")`

I understand this breaking change is annoying, but it is a Postgresql limitation, and there is no realistic way to work around it without lossing everything we've gained with this change.

What I don't quite understand though, is that unless I'm mistaken, the only valid valid for a `IS` is `NULL`. So I don't understand the need to parametise it at all.

Like how is:

```ruby
User.where('LOWER(name) IS ?', Arel.sql("NULL"))
```

Any better than just:

```ruby
User.where('LOWER(name) IS NULL')
```

Are you ever passing anything else than `NULL`?

True, but since we use parameters with other calls to keep with convention and avoid injection attacks, we kept the same form here as well.

But that leads me to the next question: Could using a full string without parameters for NULL:
```ruby
User.where('LOWER(name) IS NULL')
```
open up an app to injection attacks?

> open up an app to injection attacks?

No.

review_comments:
Thanks for the PR, but this isn't correct as it won't prepare fragment with some bound `nil` values, but:

  - That's not desirable, `nil` in bound values is fine
  - It doesn't fix the original issue if the nil bound value isn't alone, e.g. `.where("id = ? AND name IS ?", 42, nil)`
